title: tk channel command: setup telegram + status
description:
New file cmd/tk/cmd/channel.go plus registration: add "channel" to the dispatch list in cmd/tk/main.go and the cmd package dispatcher (pattern: herd/board commands).

tk channel setup telegram [--token T]:
1. Token from flag or interactive prompt (never echoed into repo files).
2. GetMe → verify token, capture bot_username.
3. Print one-time pairing code + t.me/<bot_username> link; long-poll GetUpdates until /start <code> arrives (5 min timeout).
4. Bind sender: write token/user_id/chat_id/bot_username to ~/.tick/operator.json (0600); send confirmation message to the paired chat.
5. If run inside a repo with .tick/, offer (y/N) to upsert the non-secret entry into .tick/operators.json for tk whoami's operator name.
Honors a hidden --api-base flag (and/or config) so the whole flow runs against fakebot in tests and for A31 evidence.

tk channel status: per configured channel print bot username, paired operator identity, repo mapping presence; verify token liveness with GetMe (--offline skips). Nothing configured → friendly message, exit 0.

Test cases (fakebot):
- Full pairing happy path writes both files with correct contents/permissions; wrong /start code is ignored, flow keeps waiting; timeout exits nonzero leaving no partial global config.
- status with and without config; dead token reported, exit nonzero only with --check.
- After setup: no token-shaped string anywhere under .tick/ (fact A11).
Run: go test -short -count=1 ./internal/operator/... ./cmd/tk/...
